knowledge:
- key_parameters: parser=Specifies the parser to read mzid files in PSM(); "mzR" (default) is faster and includes modification locations, while "mzID" is slower but more robust to XML variations ;; binary=Logical parameter in makeAdjacencyMatrix(); if TRUE, creates a binary adjacency matrix instead of counting peptide occurrences ;; split=Character string in makeAdjacencyMatrix() used to split protein groups (defaults to ";") ;; addCarbamidomethyl=Logical parameter in calculateFragments() and plotSpectraPTM(); if TRUE (default), automatically applies carbamidomethylation of cysteines ;; protColors=Controls protein node coloring in plotAdjacencyMatrix(); can be a numeric value (where values > 0 color proteins based on string distance of their names) or a named character vector of colors ;; pepColors=Controls peptide node coloring in plotAdjacencyMatrix(); can be NULL (white nodes) or a named character vector of colors mapped to peptide sequences
- alternatives: mzID package=Can be used as an alternative parser backend by setting parser = "mzID" in PSM() when the default mzR parser fails ;; MSnID package=Mentioned as an alternative/complementary tool to set thresholds for user-defined PSM, peptide, or protein-level FDRs
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to load and filter raw mass spectrometry identification data, resolve degenerate peptide-to-protein mappings into distinct protein groups (connected components), prioritize complex protein groups for manual inspection, or calculate and visualize theoretical fragment ions (with or without PTMs) on experimental MS2 spectra.
- pitfalls: The "mzID" parser does not extract "modLocation" information, which can cause differences in the number of filtered PSMs compared to the "mzR" parser because duplicate matches with different modification locations are collapsed ;; By default, calculateFragments() and plotSpectraPTM() apply carbamidomethylation of cysteines, which must be explicitly disabled with addCarbamidomethyl = FALSE if not present in the sample ;; joinSpectraData() may produce warnings about duplicate keys in the identification data, keeping only the last instance

workflows.name: psm_filtering_and_protein_groups
workflows.intent: Load PSM identification data, filter out low-quality matches, build an adjacency matrix, and resolve protein groups using connected components.
workflows.stages: 1. Load PSM data ;; 2. Filter PSMs ;; 3. Reduce PSMs by spectrum ID ;; 4. Build adjacency matrix ;; 5. Compute connected components ;; 6. Prioritize connected components ;; 7. Visualize adjacency matrices with custom node colors
workflows.code:
library("PSMatch")
id <- PSM(idf) |> filterPSMs()

# Alternative step-by-step filtering
id <- PSM(idf)
id <- filterPsmDecoy(id)
id <- filterPsmRank(id)
id <- filterPsmShared(id)

# Reduce PSMs by spectrum ID
id2 <- reducePSMs(id, id$spectrumID)

# Build adjacency matrix and connected components
adj <- makeAdjacencyMatrix(id)
cc <- ConnectedComponents(adj)
cx <- connectedComponents(cc, 1082)

# Visualize adjacency matrix
plotAdjacencyMatrix(cx)
plotAdjacencyMatrix(cx, 1)
plotAdjacencyMatrix(cx, 2)

# Color peptide nodes by search engine score
score <- id$MS.GF.RawScore
names(score) <- id$sequence
cls <- as.character(cut(score, 12, labels = colorRampPalette(c("white", "red"))(12)))
names(cls) <- id$sequence
plotAdjacencyMatrix(cx, pepColors = cls)

# Prioritize connected components
head(cctab <- prioritiseConnectedComponents(cc))

workflows.name: ms2_fragment_ion_analysis
workflows.intent: Calculate theoretical fragment ions for a peptide sequence and visualize them against experimental MS2 spectra.
workflows.stages: 1. Load raw MS data ;; 2. Load and filter identification data ;; 3. Merge raw and identification data ;; 4. Filter precursor scans ;; 5. Calculate theoretical fragment ions ;; 6. Plot experimental spectra and annotate with PTMs
workflows.code:
library(Spectra)
library(PSMatch)

spf <- MsDataHub::TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.20141210.mzML.gz()
sp <- Spectra(spf)

idf <- MsDataHub::TMT_Erwinia_1uLSike_Top10HCD_isol2_45stepped_60min_01.20141210.mzid()
id <- PSM(idf) |> filterPSMs()

sp <- joinSpectraData(sp, id, by.x = "spectrumId", by.y = "spectrumID")

sp1158 <- filterPrecursorScan(sp, 1158)
plotSpectra(sp1158[1], xlim = c(400, 600))
abline(v = precursorMz(sp1158)[2], col = "red", lty = "dotted")

sp1158$sequence
calculateFragments(sp1158$sequence[2], addCarbamidomethyl = FALSE)

var_seq <- PTMods::addVariableModifications(sp1158$sequence[2],
    variableModifications = c(C = 57.02146, T = 79.966)
)
calculateFragments(var_seq)

plotSpectra(sp1158[2])

dataOrigin(sp1158)[2] <- "TMT_Erwinia" ## Reduces the mzspec text
plotSpectraPTM(sp1158[2],
    fixedModifications = c(C = "Carbamidomethyl")
)

plotSpectraPTM(sp1158[2],
    variableModifications = c(C = "Carbamidomethyl"),
    addCarbamidomethyl = FALSE, ## Remove carbamidomethyl by default
    asp = 1/2,
    deltaMz = FALSE,
    main = c("Scan 1158 without carbamidomethyl", "Scan 1158 with carbamidomethyl")
)
